[Shared infrastructure]{.eyebrow}

Building shared data and code infrastructure is the first phase of the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd), and the field's most urgent near-term priority. No single existing dataset captures all seven stressor categories across multiple colonies over a full annual cycle. Closing that gap — by integrating what already exists before commissioning anything new — is where the leverage is.

## Datasets in the collaboration

| Dataset | Contributor | Contents | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-hive sensor time series | Julia Fine, USDA ARS | One year, 40 colonies, 15-minute resolution: internal acoustics, temperature, humidity, external apiary conditions; monthly manual population and brood counts | Sharing feasibility under evaluation |
| Multi-year colony measurements | Gloria DeGrandi-Hoffman, USDA ARS / ASU | Frame counts, *Varroa* levels, pollen data, virus data, organised against corresponding publications | Being organised for release |
| Dataset crosswalk / inventory | Kang, DeGrandi-Hoffman, Flenniken | Variables measured, temporal resolution, colony counts, geographic coverage, formats across all participating labs | In progress — Phase I deliverable |

## Software targets

| Tool | Lead | Description | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline colony model | Kang, Parshad, Pal | Reference implementation of the healthy-colony ODE framework with modular stressor extensions | 6 months |
| Early warning pipeline | Group 4 | Time series and machine learning pipeline for detecting pre-collapse signatures in sensor streams | 12 months |
| Beescape deep learning extension | Li, Group 5 | Deep learning on aerial imagery for flowering species richness prediction | 12 months |
| Beekeeper decision tool | Groups 2 & 4 + industry | Operational decision rules for treatment timing and split decisions | 18–24 months |

Code released by the collaboration will be published in this GitHub organisation with open licences and reproducible environments.

## External resources

- [**Beescape**](https://beescape.psu.edu/) — landscape quality assessment for pollinators (Penn State).
- [**BeeSpatial**](https://beescape.org/) — spatial pollinator habitat and forage tools.
- **BEEPOP / VarroaPop** — USDA honeybee colony population simulation models.
- [**American Institute of Mathematics**](https://aimath.org/) — host of the originating 2026 workshop.

::: {.panel}
[Contributing data]{.eyebrow}

If you hold colony monitoring data — sensor streams, inspection records, treatment logs, loss records — and would consider contributing it to the crosswalk, please [contact us](contact.qmd). Contribution to the inventory does not require making data public; the first step is simply documenting what exists.
:::
